children: Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser said on Saturday that the Fed’s December decision could spark Bitcoin’s (BTC) next rally, while calling analysts’ Nvidia (NVDA) target cuts “very, very weird.”

Speaking with Anthony Pompliano on the Pomp Podcast, Visser said, “Don’t be surprised if the catalyst for the next rally is in December, where we don’t do 50.” He was referring to Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said on Tuesday that a 50 basis point hike “should be considered” at the December meeting if October inflation came in hot, which it did.

Visser said many in the crypto community have missed how much the bond market was driving Bitcoin. He pointed to “the largest rise in two-year yields at a week, 35 basis points since 2022.” He added, “So that’s why Bitcoin is down.”
What Could Turn It Around?
For Bitcoin to recover, inflation fears should fade, allowing the Fed to stop raising rates, Visser added,

But Visser’s point stands on his explanation that Brent crude was back to its March price and inflation swaps were “at the lows of the year.” That is why he sees the Fed’s December meeting as a possible turning point.

Visser still expected the Fed to keep raising rates, saying there are “probably at least two more hikes.” His point was that a smaller increase in December, rather than a half-point hike, or 50 basis points, could be enough to spark a rally. “We need the liquidity side to turn it around,” he said.

When asked whether the AI sell-off was dragging on Bitcoin, Visser said, “Not right now. It was last week.” He explained that he thought of Bitcoin “as being two separate parts. One [was] the innovation side, and the other one [was] the liquidity side.” When the AI trade was doing well, he said, Bitcoin tended to do well with it.

Visser Is Not Buying Lower Price Targets On NVDA

Visser said that, however, Wall Street’s reaction did not add up. “Everyone lowered their price targets dramatically, but no one changed their earnings forecasts. So it’s just a very, very weird situation,” he said. He doesn’t expect Nvidia’s earnings to suffer over the next year. If the next CEO performs and growth holds, “nobody’s going to remember this in six months,” Visser said.
Nvidia is expected to release its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday.
A Wider Hit To Crypto

Fundstrat’s Tom Lee pointed to margin calls from the AI and Nvidia sell-off, “particularly Asia retail,” as one possible reason behind crypto’s weakness. Lee also urged investors to “buy the dip in $NVDA.”

Bitcoin’s price fell by over 3% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish’ zones, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

title: Jordi Visser Sees December Fed Decision As Bitcoin’s Next Catalyst, Questions Wall Street’s Nvidia Downgrades
